docs.text:
Graph Learning · Representation Learning · 3D Scene Representation

I am a researcher working on machine learning and representation learning for structured and visual data.

My established research focuses on graph neural networks, graph contrastive learning, self-supervised learning, adaptive data augmentation, negative sample selection, and robust representation learning.

My current research is expanding toward 3D scene representation and computer vision, particularly 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its extension toward semantic 3D understanding.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
I am Adnan Ali, Ph.D., currently working as a Postdoctoral Researcher at Jinan University, China. My research interests span machine learning, representation learning, graph learning, and 3D scene representation.

I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science and Technology from the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC). My doctoral research focused on graph contrastive learning for node representation and classification, with particular emphasis on data augmentation, negative sample selection, robustness, and adaptive learning strategies.

My current research is expanding toward 3D scene representation and computer vision, particularly 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its potential extensions toward semantic 3D understanding.

My broader research interests include graph neural networks, self-supervised learning, robust representation learning, computer vision, multimodal learning, and intelligent systems. I have also worked on problems involving data mining, social-network analysis, speech recognition, natural-language processing, cybersecurity, and applied machine learning.

docs.title: This Website
docs.text:
This website serves two main purposes.

First, it is my academic research profile, presenting my current research directions, publications, projects, and research interests.

Second, it is my public research and learning notebook, where I preserve practical tutorials, implementation notes, experimental workflows, technical solutions, and other useful knowledge encountered during my research and learning.

Rather than maintaining a separate technology blog, I document useful knowledge naturally as part of my research workflow. These notes primarily serve as a reference for myself, while also being openly available to researchers, students, and learners who may encounter similar problems.

docs.title: Publication Profile
docs.text:
My published work has developed from earlier research on vehicular delay-tolerant networks, security, natural-language understanding, and social-network analysis toward a stronger focus on graph representation learning and graph contrastive learning.

My recent first-author work investigates adaptive data augmentation, negative sample selection, robustness, and stability in graph contrastive learning.

docs.title: Research
docs.text: My research focuses broadly on representation learning, with particular interest in learning robust and useful representations from structured and visual data.

docs.title: Graph Representation Learning
docs.text:
A major part of my research has focused on graph neural networks and graph contrastive learning.

During my Ph.D., I investigated several challenges in self-supervised graph representation learning, including:

  • graph data augmentation
  • negative sample selection
  • adaptive training strategies
  • robustness and stability
  • node representation learning

My Ph.D. thesis focused on essential techniques of graph contrastive learning for node classification.

docs.title: Current Graph Learning Work
docs.text:
My current work in this direction includes AdNGCL, an adaptive graph contrastive learning framework that controls the exposure of negative samples during representation learning.

The framework separates the negatives available to an anchor from those actively participating in the contrastive objective and uses adaptive scheduling to regulate their contribution during training.

docs.title: 3D Scene Representation
docs.text:
My current research is also expanding toward 3D scene representation and computer vision.

I am particularly interested in:

  • 3D Gaussian Splatting
  • 3D reconstruction
  • neural rendering
  • scene representation
  • semantic 3D understanding
  • representation learning for visual environments

docs.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting
docs.text:
I am currently working with the 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline from data preparation and camera reconstruction through model training, rendering, visualization, and quantitative evaluation.

A longer-term objective is to investigate how learned semantic information can be incorporated into Gaussian-based scene representations.

docs.title: Research Direction
docs.text:
Although graph learning and 3D scene representation operate on different forms of data, both directions are connected by a common question:

How can we learn compact, robust, and useful representations of complex structured information?

My broader research interests include self-supervised learning, robust machine learning, multimodal learning, and intelligent systems.
